key_insight: A single, closed-loop framework couples a forward property predictor with an inverse generative model to design liquid electrolyte formulations; three high-conductivity candidates proposed by the system were experimentally validated.
problem_solved: Automates and accelerates electrolyte formulation by replacing slow, manual trial-and-error experimentation with a data-driven predict-then-generate workflow that targets desired properties.
method: Train a forward predictive model that maps electrolyte composition to target properties (e.g., ionic conductivity).
Use an inverse generative model to propose new formulations conditioned on desired property targets and practical constraints; rank candidates using the predictor.
Experimentally validate top candidates and feed results back to refine models (closed-loop optimization).
impact: Provides a practical blueprint for combining predictive and generative ML in materials discovery, enabling faster, cost- and time-efficient formulation optimization; approach is transferable to other chemistry and materials design problems.
visual_elements: Pipeline flowchart showing predictor → generator → candidate ranking → experimental validation (closed loop).
Predicted vs measured conductivity scatter plot with the three validated candidates highlighted.
Chemical/composition latent-space map (t-SNE or PCA) showing explored vs generated regions and candidate locations.
Bar chart comparing conductivity (and other key metrics) of baseline formulations vs the newly validated candidates.
paper_title: A unified predictive and generative solution for liquid electrolyte formulation
paper_authors: Zhenze Yang, Yifan Wu, Xu Han, Ziqing Zhang, Haoen Lai
